title: How Often Does the Field Flip?
subtitle: Teaching generative models the physics of dynamos, from a compass to the research frontier
title_options: How Often Does the Field Flip?
Exact Where It Is Exact: physics-constrained generative models for dynamos
status: outline (to be validated by the user)
logline: Nobody can say when Earth's magnetic field will flip next, but we can learn how often. One film climbs from a compass to the frontier of physics-constrained generative AI for dynamos.
synopsis: It opens on a compass and the striped seafloor, then builds the physics picture by picture: stretch versus smudge, thresholds, and liquid-sodium experiments that flip like the Earth. Chaos hides the date of the next flip, yet a shuffled box of snapshots still holds the flip rate, through Rice's formula. Generative models then learn to dream such snapshots for any knob setting. At its heart is one lesson from a prospective internship study for the MilaDy project: enforce each law where it is true, exactly for every field, or on average for the crowd. Small CPU experiments show what works and what fails. It ends on written bets for 3D dynamos, VKS and DRESDYN, filled in as simulations arrive.

chapters.title: Cold open: the needle and the stripes
chapters.learning_goal: Feel that Earth's field is not permanent: it has flipped many times, irregularly.
chapters.takeaway: The field has flipped many times, with no schedule; we can ask when, and we can ask how often.

scenes.title: A needle that settles
scenes.key_idea: A compass points north and seems permanent.
scenes.visual: Macro shot of a compass in a grey hand; the vermillion needle tip swings and settles with a 3% overshoot; slow 1.00 to 1.02 push. The polarity needle (M1) is born here; at the end of the chapter it shrinks into the top-right corner and stays for the whole film.
scenes.on_screen: none

scenes.title: Pull back to the planet
scenes.key_idea: The compass follows a field that wraps the whole planet.
scenes.visual: T2 scale dive from the hand to a landscape to Earth seen from space (plain grey sphere, no photo texture); vermillion dipole field lines bloom from pole to pole.
scenes.on_screen: chip SCHEMATIC

scenes.title: The seafloor tape recorder
scenes.key_idea: Cooling lava freezes the field's direction; spreading seafloor records it as stripes.
scenes.visual: Cross-section of a mid-ocean ridge: magma rises and cools, short vermillion grain segments align with the field and freeze, the floor slides away on two conveyor belts. Stripes accumulate mirror-symmetrically: solid vermillion = normal polarity, pale vermillion = reversed.
scenes.on_screen: labels 'normal' / 'reversed'; chip SCHEMATIC; reference chip (to be sourced)

scenes.title: Not on a schedule
scenes.key_idea: The stripes have irregular widths: the flips are irregular.
scenes.visual: Camera tilts to look down on the barcode; stripe widths visibly irregular; the barcode slides left and becomes the polarity strip under a thin D(t) trace (T1 morph).
scenes.on_screen: 'irregular: every 10^5 to 10^6 years'

scenes.title: Two questions
scenes.key_idea: When will it flip next? How often does it flip? The first is hopeless, the second is not.
scenes.visual: Two cards: 'When will it flip next?' with a grey clock, 'How often does it flip?' with amber tally marks. The clock card's border turns dashed and dims; the tally card stays lit. The altitude rail (M8) fades in on the right edge at L0.
scenes.on_screen: the two questions

scenes.title: Title
scenes.key_idea: Title card.
scenes.visual: Title words sit in a vermillion field-line field; the dipole flips and the lines reorganise around the letters; one soft impact sound.
scenes.on_screen: working title (decision D13)

chapters.title: A planet that makes its own magnet
chapters.learning_goal: Understand that the field must be regenerated by moving liquid metal, that a dynamo is a self-amplifying loop with a threshold, and that physics prefers neither polarity.
chapters.takeaway: A moving conducting fluid can turn a tiny field into a large one once its loop gain passes a threshold, and the laws do not prefer north or south.

scenes.title: No magnet inside
scenes.key_idea: The core is liquid iron and too hot to stay magnetized: the field must be continuously regenerated.
scenes.visual: Earth cutaway in grey shells (solid inner core, liquid outer core); a bar magnet glyph is heated and its arrows scatter; the outer core starts to churn (grey matter, no colour until fields appear).
scenes.on_screen: 'liquid iron outer core'; 'too hot to stay magnetized'
flags: EXTERNAL_FACT: Curie temperature of iron vs core temperature, source before use

scenes.title: Lines never end
scenes.key_idea: Magnetic field lines close on themselves: through any imaginary box, as many enter as leave.
scenes.visual: Iron filings around a bar magnet morph into vermillion field lines; a dashed box is dragged around the picture; two counters 'in' and 'out' always agree. Planted for div B = 0 (C7).
scenes.on_screen: 'lines in = lines out' (no symbol yet)

scenes.title: The squeal
scenes.key_idea: A loop with gain above one grows exponentially from almost nothing, then saturates.
scenes.visual: Microphone pointed at its own speaker: whisper, then squeal past a green gain knob (M2). Morph into a self-exciting disc: grey copper disc, coil, current arrows; below the threshold the seed dies, above it the field grows exponentially, then the plateau (the field brakes the disc).
scenes.on_screen: Predict Q2 with 3-s countdown; after the reveal: dB/dt = (gain - loss) B, so B grows like e^(lambda t)
flags: EXTERNAL_FACT: self-exciting homopolar disc (Bullard 1955), source before use
scenes.predict: Q2: spin a little faster each time: does the field grow a little each time, or nothing until a certain speed? (Answer: nothing, then exponential growth, then saturation.)

scenes.title: Who pays the bill
scenes.key_idea: A dynamo converts mechanical power into magnetic energy and heat; it creates no energy.
scenes.visual: Loop diagram: motor power -> flow (blue) -> field (vermillion) by induction -> Lorentz force brakes the flow -> heat (viscous and Joule losses, grey).
scenes.on_screen: loop labels
sources: en/prep/p3 ch. 5 loop diagram (inline SVG, redraw in palette)

scenes.title: Which way is up?
scenes.key_idea: The equations are unchanged under B -> -B: both polarities are equally lawful; which one you get is history.
scenes.visual: Predict card; then a vertical mirror plane (M10) appears; the Earth's field and its mirror twin side by side; the corner needle flips.
scenes.on_screen: Predict Q1; then 'B -> -B: same equations'
scenes.predict: Q1: physics does not care whether the field points north or south. Which polarity should Earth prefer? (Answer: neither.)

scenes.title: Checkpoint: the big picture
scenes.key_idea: Exit ramp for viewers who only wanted the big picture.
scenes.visual: Recap with motifs only (needle, barcode, squeal); the altitude rail climbs one notch, brightening to 80% for 2 s.
scenes.on_screen: 'Level 0 -> Level 1'

chapters.title: Stretch versus smudge
chapters.learning_goal: Read the induction equation as a race between stretching and diffusion; know Rm, thresholds, kinematic vs dynamic, and the ABC dynamo windows.
chapters.takeaway: A flow amplifies a field when stretching beats diffusion, and the dynamo can switch on, off, and on again.

scenes.title: Frozen threads
scenes.key_idea: A conducting flow drags field lines; stretching a line strengthens the field; diffusion smudges it.
scenes.visual: Blue tracer particles stretch and fold a vermillion material line (brightness follows stretch). Split screen: honey (threads stay sharp) vs water (a grey blur wins).
scenes.on_screen: 'stretching' / 'diffusion'

scenes.title: One number for the race
scenes.key_idea: Rm = UL/eta compares stretching with smudging; the growth rate crosses zero at a threshold.
scenes.visual: Green Rm knob turns; a schematic growth-rate curve lambda(Rm) rises through zero; the zero crossing is marked as the threshold Rm_c.
scenes.on_screen: Rm = U L / eta (U blue, eta green); chip SCHEMATIC

scenes.title: The induction equation, term by term
scenes.key_idea: The whole race in one equation.
scenes.visual: Equation built with the 10-step protocol: terms light in narrative order, leader lines to a stretched thread (advection term) and a fading thread (diffusion term).
scenes.on_screen: dB/dt = curl(u x B) + eta Laplacian(B), braces 'stretching by the flow', 'diffusion'

scenes.title: A conveyor belt that does not feel its cargo
scenes.key_idea: Kinematic dynamo: imposed flow, exponential growth (an eigenvalue problem). Dynamic: the field brakes the flow and saturates.
scenes.visual: Log plot of ||B||(t): a straight line of slope lambda (kinematic), then the same curve bending into a plateau when the Lorentz force j x B acts (dynamic). Side chip plants the anti-dynamo theorems.
scenes.on_screen: 'kinematic: B = e^(lambda t) B_hat'; chip 'anti-dynamo: no planar dynamo (Zeldovich), no axisymmetric field (Cowling)'

scenes.title: Twisting rooms: the ABC flow
scenes.key_idea: A simple periodic flow whose streamlines are corkscrews (velocity parallel to its curl).
scenes.visual: A periodic box of fat blue corkscrew streamlines (Three.js Line2), slow orbit, long lens.
scenes.on_screen: u = (A sin z + C cos y, B sin x + A cos z, C sin y + B cos x);  curl u = u

scenes.title: Predict: once on, always on?
scenes.key_idea: Dynamo windows: the ABC dynamo switches on near Rm 8.9, off near 17.6, on again above about 27.
scenes.visual: Predict card; then lambda(Rm) drawn live, left to right, from E3: 24 points, 48^3 checks as open markers, windows shaded green at 12%; inset z = 0 slices of |B| of the dominant mode at Rm 8, 12, 16, 20.
scenes.on_screen: thresholds 8.87 / 17.6 / 26.8 (32^3) vs published 8.9 / 17.5 / about 27; source chip DATA · E3
flags: CAVEAT: kinematic test bench, no generative model in E3
scenes.predict: Q3: lowering diffusion only helps stretching; once the dynamo turns on, it stays on. Right? (Answer: no, windows.)

chapters.title: Dynamos you can build, and why they are rare
chapters.learning_goal: Know why lab dynamos are hard (sodium, turbulence), what VKS showed (iron impellers, reversals), that the knob is a panel of knobs, and that simulations are too costly to cover it.
chapters.takeaway: Real dynamos depend on many knobs, flip irregularly and cost too much to simulate at every setting: we need something that fills the gaps.

scenes.title: The sodium problem
scenes.key_idea: With Pm = nu/eta about 1e-5, reaching Rm of 10 to 50 forces Re to 1e6-1e7: any lab dynamo is violently turbulent.
scenes.visual: Two gauges: Rm (green) climbs slowly, Re (blue) races; a turbulent texture fills the background.
scenes.on_screen: Pm = nu / eta ~ 1e-5;  Rm ~ 10-50 needs Re ~ 1e6-1e7

scenes.title: Three tanks that worked
scenes.key_idea: Only three liquid-sodium experiments have produced a dynamo; DRESDYN is trying with precession.
scenes.visual: Horizontal timeline cards (one moment per card): Riga (helical flow), Karlsruhe (52 helical cells), Cadarache VKS (150 litres of sodium, motors up to 300 kW); a fourth card, dashed: DRESDYN, under way.
scenes.on_screen: names and one plain line each; dates only after checking p3 ch. 6

scenes.title: VKS: two impellers and an iron surprise
scenes.key_idea: Counter-rotating impellers stir liquid sodium; the dynamo appeared only with soft-iron impellers.
scenes.visual: 3D cutaway of the cylinder (grey matter), two bladed impellers counter-rotating, blue flow cells and recirculation; the impeller material is swapped steel -> soft iron: only then does a vermillion axial dipole grow.
scenes.on_screen: chip SCHEMATIC geometry; 'stainless steel: no dynamo' / 'soft iron: dynamo'

scenes.title: VKS flips too
scenes.key_idea: With impellers at different speeds, the lab dynamo reverses irregularly, like the Earth.
scenes.visual: D(t) with reversals (qualitative curve from the VKS figure, panel b) with the barcode strip under it; corner needle flips in sync.
scenes.on_screen: '16 Hz vs 22 Hz: polarities last 120 s and 50 s on average; a reversal takes about 5 s (ohmic time about 0.4 s)'; chip 'qualitative curve'

scenes.title: A panel of knobs
scenes.key_idea: The control parameter is a vector: Re, Rm, materials, boundary conditions, forcing asymmetry, precession.
scenes.visual: The single green knob splits into a panel (Re, Rm, mu_r, asymmetry, Po). One boundary-condition switch moves the threshold marker from 90 to 130. Then the same VKS impeller wears three labels.
scenes.on_screen: 'Rm_c = 90 +/- 5 (pseudo-vacuum) -> 130 +/- 10 (vacuum)'; 'same threshold: Rm_c = 31, 44 or 52-71, three definitions'

scenes.title: A handful of dots
scenes.key_idea: Each 3D turbulent simulation is expensive, so only a few knob settings exist, each a huge dataset.
scenes.visual: A green parameter axis with a few filled dots; each dot grows a tall grey stack of data files; the gaps between dots stay empty.
scenes.on_screen: 'each simulation: a few settings, terabytes'

scenes.title: The question of this film
scenes.key_idea: Can a machine learn the family of possible fields for any knob setting, respect physics exactly where it is exact and statistically where it is statistical, and tell us how often the field flips?
scenes.visual: The question typeset word by word in the colour key (knobs green, fields blue and vermillion, 'exactly' as a single card, 'statistically' as an amber stack, 'how often' amber). Three promise chips. Project lower-third.
scenes.on_screen: central question; promises 1-3; lower-third 'MilaDy · ANR-25-CE51-0077 · since January 2026 · 48 months · LISN, Lagrange (OCA), CEREA (ENPC)'

scenes.visual: T3 ink change to PAPER; a single page card with the disclaimer, typed on.

scenes.title: Checkpoint: Level 1 done
scenes.key_idea: Exit ramp; the climb steepens.
scenes.visual: Motif recap (threads, knob panel, barcode); rail climbs to L2.
scenes.on_screen: 'Level 1 -> Level 2'

chapters.title: Chaos and the shoebox of photographs
chapters.learning_goal: See reversals in a three-mode model, understand why 'when' is unpredictable, and why the stationary distribution (a shuffled box of snapshots) is the stable object; meet crowd laws.
chapters.takeaway: The date of the next flip is unknowable, but the cloud of states is stable, and some laws hold only for the cloud.

scenes.title: Three dials
scenes.key_idea: Three coupled modes (quadrupole Q, dipole D, velocity V) with the B -> -B symmetry already reverse.
scenes.visual: Three dials (D vermillion, Q light vermillion, V blue) linked by springs; then the equations appear term by term in the same colours.
scenes.on_screen: Qdot = mu Q - V D;  Ddot = -nu D + V Q;  Vdot = Gamma - V + Q D;  (Q, D, V) -> (-Q, -D, V);  mu = 0.119, nu = 0.1; chip 'phenomenological model (Gissinger 2012)'

scenes.title: Two whirlpools and a corridor
scenes.key_idea: Below Gamma about 0.86 each trajectory is trapped in one of two mirror whirlpools; above, a corridor opens and it flips.
scenes.visual: Live RK4 integration in Canvas: (Q, D) phase portrait with a fading trail; green Gamma knob turned from 0.80 to 1.00; the two mirror whirlpools touch; a two-note sound at each crossing; scrolling magnetogram strip D(t) with its barcode underneath.
scenes.on_screen: Gamma knob value; 'merging crisis'

scenes.title: Listen to the rate
scenes.key_idea: The flip rate switches on at a threshold between Gamma = 0.86 and 0.865 and grows with Gamma.
scenes.visual: Ticks per zero crossing; the simulated crossing rate vs Gamma builds point by point (41 values); training values as filled dots.
scenes.on_screen: '0 up to 0.86 · 0.00194 per unit time at 0.865 · about 0.011 at 1.00'

scenes.title: Predict: when is the next flip?
scenes.key_idea: Errors grow by e every ~11 time units while a polarity lasts more than 100: 'when' is out of reach.
scenes.visual: Predict card; two trajectories started 1e-6 apart, drawn in two shades; their separation on a log axis climbs with slope ~0.09; a ruler compares 11 units with the >100-unit polarity length.
scenes.on_screen: 'Lyapunov time ~11 · mean polarity > 100'
scenes.predict: Q4: we know the state to six decimals. Can we predict the date of the next reversal? (Answer: no.)

scenes.title: The long exposure
scenes.key_idea: Different trajectories paint the same glow: the stationary (invariant) distribution is reproducible.
scenes.visual: Two trajectories from different starts leave long-exposure glows that converge to the same shape; an amber histogram of D (bimodal) builds below and becomes identical for both.
scenes.on_screen: 'invariant measure mu_Gamma'

scenes.title: The shoebox
scenes.key_idea: Cut the film into frames, shuffle, drop the timestamps: a sample of the stationary distribution. A snapshot does not know its own future.
scenes.visual: A film strip of the trajectory is cut into frames that fall, shuffled, into a shoebox; their time labels flutter away; the box's contents redraw the same cloud.
scenes.on_screen: 'a snapshot does not know its own future'

scenes.title: Crowd laws
scenes.key_idea: dE/dt fluctuates from snapshot to snapshot; only its mean is zero. The energy budget is a law of the crowd.
scenes.visual: Each shoebox photo drops a marble into an amber histogram of dE/dt (computed from the model's right-hand side); the histogram breathes around zero; its mean marker sits exactly at 0. A bank-account ledger flashes as a preview.
scenes.on_screen: 'true on average, not for each'; amber E[P - eps] = 0

chapters.title: Counting crossings from still photographs
chapters.learning_goal: Understand Rice's formula as 'a toll counter without a clock' and see it reproduce the true flip rate from snapshots alone.
chapters.takeaway: A shoebox of snapshots plus the equations gives the flip rate without running time forward.

scenes.title: A toll counter without a clock
scenes.key_idea: From one aerial photo with readable speedometers, count cars in a thin strip, weight by speed, divide by the width: crossings per hour.
scenes.visual: Aerial highway with a line across it; a thin strip around the line highlighted; cars inside the strip glow with their speed; a counter computes the rate; no clock anywhere.
scenes.on_screen: 'rate = (cars in strip x speed) / strip width'

scenes.title: Rice for the dipole
scenes.key_idea: For D, the strip is |D| < h and each snapshot's speed Ddot = -nu D + V Q comes from the equations.
scenes.visual: Shoebox points spread in the (D, Ddot) plane; the strip |D| < h (h = 0.2) lights up; each point's |Ddot| drawn as a bar; equation morph to the formula.
scenes.on_screen: nu_0 = lim_{h->0} (1/2h) E[ |Ddot| 1{|D|<h} ];  reference chip 'Kac 1943; Rice 1944-1945'

scenes.title: Check against the truth
scenes.key_idea: On the true distribution, with no time order, Rice reproduces direct counting within 4% near the threshold and 6% above.
scenes.visual: Rates vs Gamma: direct count (solid vermillion) and Rice on reference snapshots (amber) drawn on together.
scenes.on_screen: 'cumulative error 4% (0.865 <= Gamma <= 0.885) · 6% (Gamma >= 0.89)'; source chip DATA · E1

scenes.title: What Rice does not say
scenes.key_idea: Rice counts every zero crossing (excursions too), needs the right-hand side, gives no waiting times, and was tested on a 3-variable deterministic system.
scenes.visual: Four caveat cards slide in, one per sentence.
scenes.on_screen: four caveat cards

scenes.title: Photographs on demand
scenes.key_idea: So all we need is a cheap source of snapshots at any knob setting. Checkpoint L2 -> L3.
scenes.visual: The green parameter axis from C3.6 returns, gaps glowing; rail climbs to L3.
scenes.on_screen: 'Level 2 -> Level 3'

chapters.title: A machine that dreams snapshots
chapters.learning_goal: Understand conditional flow matching as learning an average wind from noise to data, conditioned on the knob, and how generated distributions are judged against a noise floor.
chapters.takeaway: A generative model learns a wind that carries noise to data, one model for every knob setting, judged against the noise floor.

scenes.title: From noise to data
scenes.key_idea: A wind field carries a cloud of random points onto the shape of the data.
scenes.visual: Round violet Gaussian cloud (M4); a time-dependent wind bends particle paths onto two symmetric blobs; granular hiss under the motion.
scenes.on_screen: 'generative model: new, plausible examples on demand'

scenes.title: Straight strings, average wind
scenes.key_idea: Training is plain regression: at each place and moment, learn the average direction of straight noise-to-data strings.
scenes.visual: Thousands of straight strings from noise points to data points; at a probe location the passing strings average into one violet arrow; the learned field's trajectories curve but never cross.
scenes.on_screen: x_t = (1 - t) x_0 + t x_1;  J(v) = E || v(x_t, t, lambda) - (x_1 - x_0) ||^2;  v* = E[x_1 - x_0 | x_t, lambda]

scenes.title: Turn the knob, reshape the cloud
scenes.key_idea: One model for a continuum of knob settings, including settings never simulated (interpolation).
scenes.visual: Green knob drives lambda; target blobs drift and the violet cloud follows; on the knob axis training values are filled dots, test values open dots.
scenes.on_screen: 'trained on filled dots, tested on open dots (interpolation only)'

scenes.title: Two clocks, two velocities
scenes.key_idea: The generator's time t in [0, 1] is not physical time, and its velocity v_theta (violet) is not the fluid velocity u (blue).
scenes.visual: Side-by-side chips: violet clock 't: transport time' vs grey clock 'physical time'; violet arrow v_theta vs blue arrow u.
scenes.on_screen: 'the generator makes snapshots, not movies'

scenes.title: The noise floor
scenes.key_idea: Two honest samples of the same truth differ; compare models with that floor at equal sample size, never with zero.
scenes.visual: A die rolled 1000 times, twice: two amber histograms differ; their distance becomes a dashed grey floor line. Then the energy distance built term by term over two point clouds with faint pairwise lines.
scenes.on_screen: E(P, Q) = 2 E||X - Y|| - E||X - X'|| - E||Y - Y'||; dashed 'floor'

scenes.title: A lopsided machine
scenes.key_idea: A plain conditional model reproduces the cloud's shape but inherits the training data's polarity imbalance.
scenes.visual: (Q, D) clouds at Gamma = 0.85: reference (grey, solid chip SIMULATED) vs baseline model A (violet chip GENERATED); a polarity balance bar shows A's tilt. Ends on a question mark at the mirror.
scenes.on_screen: 'Gamma = 0.85, a value never seen in training'

chapters.title: Physics, where it is true
chapters.learning_goal: Sort physical constraints into per-sample laws (build in) and crowd laws (impose on the distribution), see exact mechanisms beat penalties, equivariance beat augmentation, and per-sample enforcement of a crowd law fail.
chapters.takeaway: Enforce a constraint where it is true: build per-sample laws into every output, impose crowd laws on the crowd, never force a crowd law onto each individual.

scenes.title: Two shelves
scenes.key_idea: Taxonomy C1-C4: true for every field (C1 linear, C2 nonlinear algebraic) vs true only for the crowd (C3 symmetry, C4 stationary budgets).
scenes.visual: Two shelves; laws arrive as cards and are placed: left shelf with a single-card icon in neutral ink, right shelf with an amber card-stack icon; each shelf gets its tools. Redrawn taxonomy (no blue for per-sample).
scenes.on_screen: 'Enforce a constraint where it is true'; C1: x in ker A · C2: c(x) = 0 · C3: g#mu = mu · C4: E_mu[L phi] = 0

scenes.title: Predict: does clean data make clean outputs?
scenes.key_idea: A model trained only on divergence-free fields still outputs a relative divergence of 0.41; a soft penalty only reaches 0.34 (u) / 0.16 (B) and inflates magnetic energy 2.7x.
scenes.visual: Predict card; generated 2D MHD maps (u silver-blue, B silver-orange) reconstructed from Fourier coefficients at eta = 0.00951, free model V0 vs reference; a divergence map lights up hot spots; penalty bars follow.
scenes.on_screen: 'free: 0.41 · penalty: 0.34 (u) / 0.16 (B) · penalty E_B x2.68'; chip 'forced 2D MHD: not a dynamo (Zeldovich)'
flags: HYPOTHESIS label for 'the penalty is gamed by inflating the swirl part'
scenes.predict: Q5: trained only on perfectly divergence-free fields, are the outputs divergence-free? (Answer: no, 0.41.)

scenes.title: Hill maps and swirl minus slope
scenes.key_idea: Generate potentials (a landscape) and take the curl: zero divergence for free. Or project: remove each wave's component along its own direction.
scenes.visual: A landscape psi with water walking its contour lines (the C1.2 box returns: nothing piles up); then Fourier space: each wave's arrow loses its component along k (projector motif M6). A gauge needle drops to 1e-17.
scenes.on_screen: u = (d_y psi, -d_x psi);  u_k -> (I - k k^T / |k|^2) u_k;  gauges: final projection 5e-17 · potentials 1.7e-17 · projected flow 2e-8 (single precision)

scenes.title: Why almost is not exactly
scenes.key_idea: The ideal wind must squeeze the off-constraint part at a rate 1/(1 - t) that blows up at the end; a bounded network cannot.
scenes.visual: T3 ink change to PAPER; plot of 1/(1 - t) shooting up near t = 1, with a capped curve for a bounded network; the residual gap stays O(1).
scenes.on_screen: Prop. 2: v* = m(P x, t) - (I - P) x / (1 - t); Remark 3.6

scenes.title: Predict: the mirror test
scenes.key_idea: Augmentation symmetrizes only where data exist; a mirror built into the network keeps both polarities equally likely at every knob value.
scenes.visual: Predict card; training data lopsided below threshold (P(D > 0) = 0.375 at Gamma 0.80, 0.3125 at 0.86). Asymmetry vs Gamma for A, B, C drawn per Gamma (train filled, test open): A spikes, B dips only at training values, C sits on the dashed floor. Then (Q, D) clouds A vs C at 0.85 and the mirror gate S acting on the violet cloud.
scenes.on_screen: 'A: 0.183 at 0.86, 0.085 at unseen 0.87 · B: 0.020-0.025 between training values · C: about 0.004 (floor) everywhere'; v_sym = 1/2 [v(x) + S v(S x)], S = diag(-1, -1, 1)
scenes.predict: Q6: one student learns from mirrored copies, the other has a mirror built in. At an unseen knob value, who stays symmetric? (Answer: the built-in mirror.)

scenes.title: The budget is blind to the mirror
scenes.key_idea: Any mixture of the two polarities satisfies the energy identities, so symmetry must be imposed separately.

opening_60s.tts_text: [calm, natural narrator voice] Hold a compass. The needle swings, hesitates, and settles. North. It has pointed north your whole life. It feels permanent. [long pause] It is not. Along the ridges of the ocean floor, fresh lava cools, and tiny magnetic grains freeze in place. Each grain remembers which way a compass would have pointed. As the seafloor spreads, these memories line up into stripes. And the stripes tell a strange story. The field has flipped. Not once. Many times. With no schedule at all. [long pause] So, two questions. When will it flip next? And how often does it flip? The first question turns out to be hopeless. The second one is not. Finding out why will take us from this needle to liquid metal, to chaos, and to machines that must be taught where the laws of physics are exact, and where they only hold on average.
opening_60s.notes: The seafloor sentences rely on an external fact (decision D7). Site-only alternative for C0.3: 'In a tank of liquid sodium in Cadarache, the field flips too.'

closing_60s.tts_text: [calm, natural narrator voice] Back to the compass in your hand. [long pause] We still cannot tell you when this needle will turn around. Nobody can. The dynamo below is chaotic. Its memory fades too fast. But it does answer another question: how often. That answer hides in a cloud of snapshots, and a machine can learn to draw such clouds, even at settings nobody has simulated. [long pause] On small test problems, it partly works. The mirror symmetry holds by construction. On a three-variable model, the flip rate comes out with a cumulative error of fourteen percent far from the threshold, and forty-two percent near it. The real tests, in three dimensions and in liquid metal, are still ahead. You have seen the bets. [long pause] One lesson remains. Enforce each law where it is true. Exactly, where it is exact. On average, where it only holds on average.
closing_60s.notes: Numbers follow pitfall P15 (cumulative error, two regimes). 'Holds by construction' refers to Proposition 4.
